title: Distance across time is native as a cone; cuts count the ring graph's distance
claim: For every network of rule-60 rings with law (12,12) contacts (no two corners of one length between the same two contacts): (1) a chordless route of L arcs from ring X to contact c, isolated by freezing every contact off it, makes c first need X at lag 1 + the cells its hops carry (g L + 1 at spacing g), first lags add when routes are joined, and an induced route's need set is {T : C(T - L - 1, sum of own cells + m) odd for some m < own cells of X's corner}, with every route contact binding both rings at every lag (composition at recurring lags, A37); (2) the earliest lag at which any freeze set makes c need X is 1 + lambda(X -> c), the least cells of a route (g delta + 1, delta the contact graph's directed distance), and delta is a directed metric between contacts, not symmetric; (3) the most pairwise disjoint freeze sets leaving rings X and Y in different native pieces is the ring graph's distance D(X, Y), and the most pairwise disjoint sets blocking c from X for good is delta(X -> c); (4) the plain first need kappa >= delta, with equality exactly when an odd number of shortest routes arrive from one contact of X; on the square torus closed forms for delta, D = ceil(delta/2) for every ring and contact, and for contacts of one kind at offset (a, b), |a|, |b| < n/2, the need on time iff a AND b = 0; on the plane offsets with v2(a) = v2(b) never needed (density 1/3) and kappa doubling; (5) between a contact and its translate by a lattice vector v, delta = (m/2) D(0, v) on the square, triangular and honeycomb tori (m = 4, 6, 3). Computed: D = ceil(delta/3) on triangular tori of side 4 to 10, ceil(3D/2) - 1 <= delta <= ceil(3D/2) on honeycomb tori of side 3 to 9; the plain first need breaks the triangle inequality (contact to contact on every network checked, ring to ring on all but the tetrahedron).
failure_conditions: An isolated chordless route whose far contact first needs the near ring at a lag other than 1 + the cells it carries.
A freeze set that makes a contact need a ring before 1 + lambda, or a fewest-cells fewest-arcs route that does not give exactly 1 + lambda when isolated.
More than D(X, Y) pairwise disjoint sets separating two rings into different native pieces, or more than delta(X -> c) blocking for good.
A ring-contact pair whose plain first need is on time without an odd count of shortest routes, or late with one.
A contact and its translate whose directed distance is not (m/2) times the ring graph's distance.
foundation_claim_scope: Networks of rule-60 rings with law (12,12) contacts, given rather than grown; counted lengths across time under A40, read through needs and freezes (A32, A38); two-time knots only (A30). Not the foundation's minimal contact-distance, and no coordinate, angle or embedding is read from the substrate.
